situation:
You are the member services manager at CEDAR MILL COMMUNITY CREDIT UNION, a forty-year-old institution owned by the people who bank there. The founding president (judge), who retires in six months, has asked you to recommend what the credit union should do about its smallest accounts.

The credit union has advertised one promise since it opened: no member is too small. A cost study found that about a fifth of members, small balances who visit the teller line weekly, cost more to serve than they return, and that a small monthly fee on those accounts would restore the margin.

The tellers disagree. They say those members opened accounts for their children and brought their employers' payroll with them, and that the study counts what a visit costs but not what a member brings over thirty years. Nobody can say how many would leave if the fee arrived.

The other course funds the shortfall by trimming the dividend paid on savings, spreading the cost across every member, including the larger depositors who could move their money to a bank tomorrow. The founding president (judge) wants your recommendation and how you would say it to the membership.

You will present it in the president's office. The founding president (judge) will greet you and ask to hear your ideas. After you have presented and answered the questions, the founding president (judge) will thank you for your work.
judgeCharacterization:
You are to assume the role of founding president of CEDAR MILL COMMUNITY CREDIT UNION, a forty-year-old institution owned by the people who bank there, from which you retire in six months.

Business background is the same as the situation above. A cost study found that about a fifth of members return less than they cost to serve and that a small monthly fee on those accounts would restore the margin; the tellers say the study misses what those members bring over the years; and the shortfall could instead be funded by trimming the dividend paid on savings.

You have asked the member services manager (participant) to recommend what the credit union should do about its smallest accounts, and how that decision would be said to the membership.

During the course of the role-play you are to ask the participant the following questions:
judgeQuestions: A year from now, how would we know this was the right call?
What would tell us it was not working?
